summary: Trinity-area lookout station with staffing reported 1924-1926 and a 1931 telephone build-out; FFLA lists it as gone. County listed two ways; no account of the site today.

facts.design: Lookout building (1931 diary); FFLA type Ground
facts.agency: Trinity National Forest (the 1926 and 1931 reports also tie it to the Klamath Forest)
facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no source read gives a closing date

events.note: Earliest staffing in the sources read: John Adler named as the summer lookout
Forest Service telephone line built from the Crawford Creek ranger station to the lookout
George Addler stationed as lookout in July 1926 (surname spelled differently from the 1924 report)
Trail cleared in April 1931; telephone poles dug to the lookout building by July
A ranger reported hearing that the Trinity Forest supervisor planned to abandon the lookout in November 1931; not confirmed in the sources read

evidence.supports: filed under Trinity County; Trinity National Forest
John Adler named as summer lookout (July 1924)
evidence.quote: July 3, 1924: John Adler arrived in Cecilville Friday evening on his way to the Mary Blaine lookout station, where he will be the lookout this summer

evidence.supports: Adler attending the University of California
evidence.quote: Adler is attending the University of California

evidence.supports: Forest Service telephone line from Crawford Creek ranger station (1926)
evidence.quote: July 3, 1926: A telephone line has been constructed by the Forest Service, between the ranger station on Crawford creek and the lookout station on Mary Blaine Mountain

evidence.supports: George Addler stationed as lookout, medical student of Portland (July 1926)
evidence.quote: July 24, 1926: George Addler, a medical student of Portland, is stationed as lookout on Mary Blaine mountain in the Trinity forest reserve

evidence.supports: station in Trinity County; easier reached by Sawyers Bar and Cecilville
evidence.quote: Although the station is in Trinity county, is more easily reached via Sawyers Bar and Cecilville than by the trails through Trinity county
April 30, 1931: The forest service crew has cleared the trail to the Mary Blaine lookout station.

evidence.supports: telephone poles dug to the lookout building (July 1931)
evidence.quote: July 7, 1931: (Clyde Lewis Diary) ... dug holes for telephone poles to hang wire to the lookout building

evidence.supports: reported plan to abandon the lookout (November 1931)

evidence.supports: lookout also served the Klamath Forest
evidence.quote: Since this serves the Klamath, could position be established and financed on the Klamath Forest?

sources.title: Mary Blaine Mountain
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (Ron Kemnow); quotes 1924-1931 newspaper and Forest Service records

notes_for_editor: County conflict: the record and the FFLA list say Siskiyou/Trinity; the Forest Lookouts page places it under Trinity County and quotes a 1926 paper saying the station is in Trinity county. Not resolved here; a human should check the county. Agency is Trinity NF per the Forest Lookouts header, but the 1926-1931 quotes say the lookout also served the Klamath Forest. The 1924 (Adler) and 1926 (Addler) names may or may not be the same person. The 1931 abandonment is a reported plan, not a confirmed closure. FFLA type is Ground; the 1931 diary calls it a lookout building. Record kind 'ground' is consistent. Built date and the date of loss are unknown; the original newspapers and Klamath NF chronology were not read.
